hypha.definition: n any of the threadlike filaments forming the mycelium of a fungus

hyphae.definition:
n. pl. The long, branching filaments of which the mycelium
   (and the greater part of the plant) of a fungus is formed. They are
   also found enveloping the gonidia of lichens, making up a large part of
   their structure.

hyphema.definition: n bleeding into the interior chamber of the eye
hyphema.translation: 眼前房出血, 眼前房积血

hyphen.definition: n. a punctuation mark (-) used between parts of a compound word or between the syllables of a word when the word is divided at the end of a line of text
hyphen.translation:
n. 连字符
vt. 用连字符连接

hyphenated.definition: v divide or connect with a hyphen

hyphenates.definition: v divide or connect with a hyphen
hyphenates.translation: v. 以连字符号连接（hyphenate的第三人称单数形式）

hyphogenous.translation: [医] 菌丝原的, 菌丝性的

hyphomycetes.definition:
n. pl. One of the great division of fungi, containing
   those species which have naked spores borne on free or only fasciculate
   threads.
hyphomycetes.translation: [医] 丝状菌类, 不[完]全菌纲

hyphy.definition:
Main Entry: hyphy\r
Pronunciation: "HIGH-fee"\r
Function: adjective\r
 \r
Etymology: Etymology: San Francisco Bay Area, shortened perhaps from English dialect "hyperactive"; other sources cite a combination of "hype" and "fly." Popularized by E-40 and the Federation's song "Hyphy" (2004); first known use on record by Keak Da Sneak in 1998 (on "Cool," from his LP Sneakacidle).\r
1 : dangerous and irrational: CRAZY;\r
2 : amusingly eccentric; without inhibition: GOOFY
> "They were getting hyphy up in the club Saturday night."
